info.description:
The API of Platita, a personal and family finance assistant. The dashboard is its only client, and both are served from one origin.

**Session.** It travels in the cookie `__Host-sid`, which the page cannot read. An operation that asks for a session is marked as such, and answers `401` without a valid one.

**Requests that change something.** A `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` must come from the page of the API itself and be JSON: with another `Origin`, without one, or with another `Content-Type`, it answers `403`.

**Errors.** Every error has the same body: its code in `error`, a short lowercase word that never changes. Every response carries the header `X-Request-Id`, the reference to look for in the logs.
info.title: Platita

get.description: The accounts of the user of the session, each with its balance computed from its movements and transfers dated up to today, in the time zone of the user. The balance is never stored. They come first in the primary currency of the user, then in the other currencies by code, and within each currency by name. An account of type `receivable` is money others owe the user: the dashboard does not list it with the others.

200.description: The accounts of the user. An empty list when there are none.

401.description: There is no valid session: missing, unknown, revoked or expired, told apart nowhere.

get.summary: List the accounts and their balance

403.description: The request did not come from the page of the API itself, or it is not JSON. Nothing of what it sent was read.

get.description: The periods the user of the session can read: their own, every period of the groups they are a current member of, and of a group they left, the ones that overlap their membership. Each one with its limits, whether the user can edit it, and whether it covers today, in the time zone of the user. The one that starts latest comes first; with the same start, the individual one before those of groups, by name.

401.description: There is no valid session: missing, unknown, revoked or expired, told apart nowhere.

With `after`, only the ones that come after that message: it is what the dashboard asks every few seconds. It does not count as activity of the session.

post.description: Stores the message as written by the user of the session, and answers at once without processing it. The reply of Platita is not here: it shows up later in `GET /chat/messages`. The time of the message is the one the server received it at.

401.description: There is no valid session: missing, unknown, revoked or expired, told apart nowhere.

403.description: The request did not come from the page of the API itself, or it is not JSON. Nothing of what it sent was read.

422.description: The text is empty or only spaces, or the header `Idempotency-Key` is missing.

post.description: Opens a real session without a login code and returns it in the session cookie. In the local environment the user is chosen from the list, with `user_id`. A personal link, with `access_token`, is the way in of the demo environment and is not built yet: it answers `404`. One of the two is required.

204.description: The session was opened. Its token is in the cookie, and the body is empty.

403.description: The request did not come from the page of the API itself, or it is not JSON. Nothing of what it sent was read.

404.description: The development entry is disabled, the user does not exist or is not a test user, `user_id` was sent outside the local environment, or the personal link is unknown. The same answer for all of them.

422.description: Neither `user_id` nor `access_token` was sent, or `user_id` is not a UUID.

get.description: The users anyone may enter as: the ones with an invented phone, which starts with `+000`. A user with a real phone is never listed. It asks for no session. It exists only in the local environment.

404.description: The development entry is disabled, or the environment is not local.

get.description: Answers as long as the process runs. It does not touch the database.
The user of the session of the request. The dashboard asks this when it loads, because it cannot read the cookie. It counts as activity of the session.

401.description: There is no valid session: missing, unknown, revoked or expired, told apart nowhere.

get.description: Fails when a pending message has waited longer than the configured wait to be processed: 10 minutes, unless `QUEUE_MAX_WAIT_MINUTES` says otherwise. A message delayed on purpose does not count. It is what the external monitor watches, because the worker may hang while the API is healthy.

200.description: No pending message has waited longer than the configured wait.

503.description: A pending message has waited longer than the configured wait, or the database does not answer. The body has the same shape as the `200`.

get.summary: Does the worker keep up with the messages

get.description: Asks the database the cheapest question there is. It is what a deployment waits for before sending requests.
